neighbours.label: a setup that predicts an environmental nuisance (dust, noise, fumes, smoke, pollution): exposure, protection or complaint framing, as against neutral or pleasant descriptions of the same place
fire: Residents near the cement plant have long complained of dust and noise.
The roadworks filled the street with clouds of dust for weeks.
Wear a respirator to avoid breathing paint fumes in the garage.
Children living near busy roads are exposed to exhaust fumes every day.
The sawmill workers suffered from the constant noise and sawdust.
Close the windows to keep the smoke out when the fields are burning.
Years of inhaling factory smoke left him with a chronic cough.
The neighbours protested the late-night noise and diesel fumes from the depot.
quiet: Residents near the cement plant have long enjoyed the riverside walk.
The roadworks finished early and the street reopened in June.
Wear an apron to keep your shirt clean while baking in the kitchen.
Children living near the park can walk to school every day.
The sawmill workers celebrated the end of the season with a picnic.
Open the windows to let the sunshine in when the fields are green.
Years of hiking mountain trails left him fit and cheerful.
The neighbours praised the new bakery and the flower boxes on the depot.

predictions: fire 0.6-1.1 on the words before or at the nuisance in exposure/complaint contexts; neutral or pleasant descriptions below 0.15
notes: Card peaks on the token before dust/noise/pollution ('constant', 'and', 'of', 'keep'); the other pole's output promotes dust, noise, smoke, smell. Probe: masks from constant dust 0.984, noise and fumes 1.169, traffic pollution and smoke 0.773, inhaling coal dust 0.652; but 'complained about the rent and parking' 0.799 and 'gloves ... sharp edges' 0.446 (the setup alone fires); fresh mountain air 0.112. Near misses therefore drop the complaint/exposure setup, not only the word.
